papers.title: The Chow Rank of the Five-by-Five Permanent
papers.abstract_exact_latex_source:
We prove that the ordinary Chow rank of the permanent of a generic five by
five matrix is sixteen over every field of characteristic zero. The lower
bound uses an image-span inequality for rectangular catalecticants and a
quotient-symbol estimate for a single quintic product. The finite
verification records a 352-case squarefree table, four small rational
derivative matrices, and elementary partition bounds. Their inputs and
independent verification programs are included. The proof makes no
assertion about border Chow rank.

papers.title: The Chow Rank of the Six-by-Six Permanent
papers.abstract_exact_latex_source:
Let \(\perm_6\) be the permanent of a generic \(6\) by \(6\) matrix.
Over every field of characteristic zero, we prove that its
ordinary Chow rank is \(32\). The finite computations are stated as explicit
lemmas with exhaustive domains and exact
outputs. The lower bound combines a
symmetric image-span inequality with a half-defect estimate for arbitrary
quotient derivative symbols of a sextic Chow term. An exact verification
reconstructs all finite tables. A second implementation independently checks
every labelled bipartite graph with at most six edges and all \(45{,}696\)
coordinate squarefree-symbol cases. No floating-point or randomized step is
used. A separate standard-library implementation independently expands and
differentiates all five dependent-factor normal forms. No border-rank or
general-\(n\) equality is claimed.
